challenge.better_approach: Considered reconciling a one-component run against only the sieves it fired. That still cannot clear anything, because a per-sieve identity spans components, so skipping is the whole of it.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a one-component run is ever used. The module docstring names it as the post-build run, so the path is live by its own contract.
challenge.prior_art: Ticket 9579a6f9cec6 moved the reconcile to trouble's side; cd27b72ba964 made identities per sieve. Neither scoped the reconcile to the whole-repo run. The proof test_finding_baseline_reconcile.py pins the set, not who may send it.
challenge.real_collision: None. The whole-repo run keeps its reconcile unchanged.

answers.falsifier: A one-component run emits no reconcile and still raises its own finding; the whole-repo run still reconciles every sieve above baseline.
answers.from_idea: none, because this was measured, not imagined: _main in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py reconciles the whole inspector-new-finding- prefix after a run narrowed to one component
answers.how: In _main of cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py, call _reconcile_cleared_findings only when no component was named. A red-first proof drives _main with a scripted inspect and a recording raiser.
answers.traces_to: Law 7: a trouble cleared while its cause stands is a quiet wrong. Ticket cd27b72ba964 made a finding trouble one per sieve, so a narrowed run cannot speak for other components.
answers.what: A build-inspector run over one component clears no finding trouble; only a run that saw every component reconciles.

bullets.text: A one-component inspector run reconciles every finding trouble against one component's findings, so it would clear troubles still firing elsewhere. Measured red on origin/main.

title: A build-inspector run over one component clears no finding trouble; only a run that saw every component reconciles.
